<a name="BulkWriter"></a>
## type [BulkWriter](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/bulk.go#L14-L19>)

BulkWriter stages graph insertions in one atomic Database.BulkUpdate. It caches node\-existence checks so edges that share endpoints do not repeatedly probe the same node records. A BulkWriter is valid only during its callback and must not be used concurrently.

```go
type BulkWriter struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="BulkWriter.BindExternalID"></a>
### func \(\*BulkWriter\) [BindExternalID](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/bulk.go#L70>)

```go
func (w *BulkWriter) BindExternalID(externalID ExternalID, nodeID uuid.UUID) error
```

BindExternalID binds an external identity to a node in the current bulk transaction. Repeating the same binding is idempotent.

<a name="BulkWriter.PutEdge"></a>
### func \(\*BulkWriter\) [PutEdge](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/bulk.go#L84>)

```go
func (w *BulkWriter) PutEdge(srcID, dstID uuid.UUID, label string) (uuid.UUID, error)
```

PutEdge stages a directed edge after validating its endpoints. Each distinct endpoint is read at most once during the bulk callback; nodes inserted through this writer require no additional endpoint read.

```go
func (w *BulkWriter) PutNode(id uuid.UUID, label string) error
```

PutNode stages a node upsert and makes the node immediately available to later PutEdge calls in the same bulk callback.

<a name="Database"></a>
## type [Database](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L90-L97>)

Database represents a connection to the embedded graph database. It is safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines.

```go
type Database struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Open"></a>
### func [Open](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L108>)

```go
func Open(path string) (*Database, error)
```

Open creates or opens a graph database at the given path with default options.

Usage:

```
// Open a database on disk
db, err := pathway.Open("data/graph.db")

// Open an in-memory database (useful for testing)
db, err := pathway.Open(":memory:")
```

<a name="OpenWithOptions"></a>
### func [OpenWithOptions](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L118>)

```go
func OpenWithOptions(path string, opts Options) (*Database, error)
```

OpenWithOptions opens the database with specific options. It takes an owned snapshot of mutable option containers, so it never applies defaults or in\-memory overrides to caller\-owned configuration and one Options value may be reused by concurrent opens. In addition to logging, monitoring hooks, and Pebble settings, options configure write durability and persisted exact\-match node\-property indexes.

<a name="Database.BulkUpdate"></a>
### func \(\*Database\) [BulkUpdate](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/bulk.go#L25>)

```go
func (d *Database) BulkUpdate(ctx context.Context, fn func(writer *BulkWriter) error) error
```

BulkUpdate stages nodes, edges, and properties in one transaction and commits them once with the database's configured durability. Any writer operation or callback error rolls back the complete batch, including errors the callback did not explicitly return.

<a name="Database.Close"></a>
### func \(\*Database\) [Close](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L187>)

```go
func (d *Database) Close() error
```

Close closes the database connection and releases all resources. It is important to call Close\(\) to ensure all data is flushed to disk \(if persistent\) and locks are released.

<a name="Database.Compact"></a>
### func \(\*Database\) [Compact](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L274>)

```go
func (g *Database) Compact(ctx context.Context) error
```

Compact triggers Pebble's manual compaction for the entire key range. It can be used to reclaim disk space after deleting a large number of nodes or edges. Note: This operation can be expensive and should typically not be run during high load.

<a name="Database.Update"></a>
### func \(\*Database\) [Update](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L201>)

```go
func (d *Database) Update(ctx context.Context, fn func(tx *Tx) error) error
```

Update executes a function within a read\-write transaction. The transaction is committed if the function returns nil, or rolled back if it returns an error. Commit synchronization follows Options.Durability; the default is DurabilitySync.

Usage:

```
err := db.Update(ctx, func(tx *pathway.Tx) error {
    return tx.PutNode(uuid.New(), "Person")
})
```

<a name="Database.View"></a>
### func \(\*Database\) [View](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L232>)

```go
func (d *Database) View(ctx context.Context, fn func(tx *Tx) error) error
```

View executes a function within a read\-only transaction. The transaction provides a consistent snapshot of the database at the start of the call. It is automatically rolled back after the function returns.

Usage:

```
err := db.View(ctx, func(tx *pathway.Tx) error {
    node, exists, err := tx.GetNode(id)
    // ...
    return nil
})
```

<a name="DurabilityMode"></a>
## type [DurabilityMode](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L34>)

DurabilityMode controls whether Update synchronizes its commit to stable storage before returning.

```go
type DurabilityMode uint8
```

<a name="DurabilitySync"></a>

```go
const (
    // DurabilitySync synchronizes every successful Update. This is the default
    // and protects committed updates from process and machine crashes.
    DurabilitySync DurabilityMode = iota

    // DurabilityNoSync skips the commit sync. Updates remain atomic and become
    // visible immediately, but recent successful updates may be lost after a
    // process or machine crash. Use it only when the source data can be replayed.
    DurabilityNoSync
)
```

<a name="ExternalID"></a>
## type [ExternalID](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/external_id.go#L25-L29>)

ExternalID is an immutable, namespaced identifier owned by an external data source. Namespace is exact, case\-sensitive UTF\-8; Pathway performs no Unicode normalization. Scope and Value are opaque bytes compared exactly. Scope may be empty, while Namespace and Value must contain 1..MaxExternalIDPartBytes bytes.

Use distinct namespaces for identifiers with different canonical forms. For example, Git SHA\-1 and SHA\-256 object IDs should use different namespaces and store the raw digest in Value. Repository\-local identities should put the canonical repository identity in Scope instead of concatenating it with the digest.

```go
type ExternalID struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Iterator"></a>
## type [Iterator](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/iterator.go#L20-L28>)

Iterator is the common lifecycle contract for graph and traversal results.

Call Next before reading each result. A true return positions the iterator on one result until the next call to Next. False means iteration has ended; callers must then check Error. Close releases iterator resources and must be called once on every iterator, including empty and failed iterators. Close ends the iterator lifetime; no methods may be called afterward. Iterators are not safe for concurrent use. An iterator returned by Tx must be closed before its transaction closes.

```go
type Iterator interface {
    // Next advances to the next result. It returns false on exhaustion or error.
    Next() bool
    // Close releases all resources owned by the iterator.
    Close() error
    // Error reports construction or advancement errors. It is checked after
    // Next returns false and does not report exhaustion as an error.
    Error() error
}
```

<a name="Options"></a>
## type [Options](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/database.go#L56-L86>)

Options configuration for the database.

Example:

```
opts := pathway.Options{
    OnQueryStart: func(ctx context.Context, query string) {
        fmt.Printf("Starting query: %s\n", query)
    },
}
```

```go
type Options struct {
    // OnQueryStart is called before a query executes.
    // This is useful for auditing or tracing query execution.
    OnQueryStart func(ctx context.Context, query string)

    // OnQueryEnd is called after execution, providing duration and error/success status.
    // This is useful for monitoring performance and logging slow queries.
    OnQueryEnd func(ctx context.Context, query string, duration time.Duration, err error)

    // Logger interface for internal debug logs.
    // If nil, no internal logging will be performed.
    Logger Logger

    // PebbleOptions allows customizing the underlying storage engine
    // (cockroachdb/pebble). OpenWithOptions clones this value before applying
    // defaults or in-memory overrides. Use it to tune cache sizes, compaction
    // settings, or file system options.
    PebbleOptions *pebble.Options

    // Durability controls Update commit synchronization. The zero value is
    // DurabilitySync. DurabilityNoSync improves write throughput by allowing
    // Pebble to buffer recent WAL writes in memory, so acknowledged updates may
    // be lost after a process or machine crash.
    Durability DurabilityMode

    // Indexes is the desired set of node-property indexes. A nil slice preserves
    // definitions already stored in an existing database (and creates none for a
    // new database); a non-nil empty slice removes every index. Added indexes are
    // built and removed indexes are dropped atomically while opening the database.
    Indexes []IndexDefinition
}
```

## type [Path](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L51>)

Path is an ordered snapshot of the elements visited by a traversal result.

```go
type Path []PathElement
```

<a name="PathElement"></a>
## type [PathElement](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L43-L48>)

PathElement is one typed node or edge in a traversal path. Other is set for edges and identifies the endpoint reached by that traversal step.

```go
type PathElement struct {
    Kind  PathElementKind
    ID    uuid.UUID
    Label string
    Other uuid.UUID
}
```

<a name="PathElementKind"></a>
## type [PathElementKind](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L34>)

PathElementKind identifies the graph element represented by a path entry.

```go
type PathElementKind string
```

<a name="PathNode"></a>

```go
const (
    PathNode PathElementKind = "node"
    PathEdge PathElementKind = "edge"
)
```

<a name="Predicate"></a>
## type [Predicate](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/predicates.go#L17>)

Predicate tests a dynamic property value. Values can be nil, bool, int64, uint64, float64, string, \[\]byte, \[\]any, or map\[string\]any, matching the documented Values and GetProperties result contract.

```go
type Predicate func(any) bool
```

<a name="Contains"></a>
### func [Contains](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/predicates.go#L165>)

```go
func Contains(substr string) Predicate
```

Contains returns a predicate that checks if a string contains substr.

<a name="Eq"></a>
### func [Eq](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/predicates.go#L25>)

```go
func Eq(expected any) Predicate
```

Eq returns a predicate that checks for deep, type\-sensitive equality. It is safe for byte slices, lists, and maps.

Usage:

```
pathway.Eq("Person")
```

<a name="Gt"></a>
### func [Gt](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/predicates.go#L38>)

```go
func Gt(expected any) Predicate
```

Gt returns a predicate that checks whether a numeric value is greater than expected. All signed integer, unsigned integer, and floating\-point Go types are compared by exact numeric value. Unsupported types and NaN do not match.

Usage:

```
pathway.Gt(18)
```

<a name="Lt"></a>
### func [Lt](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/predicates.go#L51>)

```go
func Lt(expected any) Predicate
```

Lt returns a predicate that checks whether a numeric value is less than expected. It has the same numeric conversion contract as Gt.

Usage:

```
pathway.Lt(100.0)
```

<a name="Prefix"></a>
### func [Prefix](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/predicates.go#L155>)

```go
func Prefix(prefix string) Predicate
```

Prefix returns a predicate that checks if a string starts with prefix.

Usage:

```
pathway.Prefix("User-")
```

<a name="RepeatConfig"></a>
## type [RepeatConfig](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L169-L183>)

RepeatConfig holds configuration for repeat steps \(loops\).

```go
type RepeatConfig struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="RepeatVisitMode"></a>
## type [RepeatVisitMode](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L148>)

RepeatVisitMode controls how Repeat treats a node reached through more than one traversal path.

```go
type RepeatVisitMode uint8
```

<a name="RepeatDeduplicateNodes"></a>

```go
const (
    // RepeatDeduplicateNodes visits each node UUID at most once. It is the
    // default and produces one breadth-first result for converging paths.
    RepeatDeduplicateNodes RepeatVisitMode = iota
    // RepeatPathSensitive preserves distinct simple paths to the same node.
    // Revisiting a node already present in the current path is suppressed, so
    // cycles remain finite.
    RepeatPathSensitive
)
```

<a name="Snapshot"></a>
## type [Snapshot](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/snapshot.go#L12-L14>)

Snapshot represents a read‑only view of the database at a point in time. It holds a Pebble snapshot which guarantees a consistent view even while writes are occurring.

```go
type Snapshot struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Snapshot.Close"></a>
### func \(\*Snapshot\) [Close](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/snapshot.go#L27>)

```go
func (s *Snapshot) Close() error
```

Close releases the snapshot resources.

<a name="Snapshot.Get"></a>

```go
func (s *Snapshot) Get(key []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

Get returns a Pebble reader that can be used to read keys from the snapshot.

<a name="Step"></a>
## type [Step](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L144>)

Step defines a processing step in the traversal pipeline. It takes a transaction context and a previous iterator, and returns a new iterator.

```go
type Step func(tx *Tx, prev Iterator) Iterator
```

<a name="Traversal"></a>
## type [Traversal](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L15-L16>)

Traversal represents a fluent query builder. Currently empty but kept for type safety and potential future state.

```go
type Traversal struct {
}
```

<a name="TraversalPipeline"></a>
## type [TraversalPipeline](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L210-L216>)

TraversalPipeline represents a chain of query steps.

```go
type TraversalPipeline struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="TraversalPipeline.AllowUnboundedRepeat"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [AllowUnboundedRepeat](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L443>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) AllowUnboundedRepeat() *TraversalPipeline
```

AllowUnboundedRepeat explicitly permits the active Repeat to run without an Until predicate or Times limit. It must immediately follow Repeat or another repeat modifier and cannot be combined with a termination policy. Both visit modes suppress cycles, but callers should still use a cancellable context for large traversals.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.Each"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [Each](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L515>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) Each(ctx context.Context, yield func(any) error) (err error)
```

Each executes the traversal pipeline and calls yield once for every result. It streams results without retaining them, so memory use does not grow with the traversal size. Returning an error from yield stops iteration; the error is returned after all traversal resources have been closed. Cancellation is checked while building and advancing the traversal.

Unprojected nodes and edges are passed as Node and Edge values. IDs emits uuid.UUID, Path emits Path, and Values emits the dynamic property types documented by Predicate. The values passed to yield own their data and remain valid after yield returns. Prefer a typed EachNode, EachEdge, EachPath, or EachID terminal for statically typed results.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.EachEdge"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [EachEdge](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L527>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) EachEdge(ctx context.Context, yield func(Edge) error) error
```

EachEdge executes an edge traversal and calls yield for every Edge. It returns ErrTraversalResult when the final pipeline step emits another type.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.EachID"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [EachID](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L540>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) EachID(ctx context.Context, yield func(uuid.UUID) error) error
```

EachID executes a traversal ending in IDs and calls yield for every UUID. It returns ErrTraversalResult when the final pipeline step emits another type.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.EachNode"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [EachNode](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L521>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) EachNode(ctx context.Context, yield func(Node) error) error
```

EachNode executes a node traversal and calls yield for every Node. It returns ErrTraversalResult when the final pipeline step emits another type.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.EachPath"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [EachPath](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L534>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) EachPath(ctx context.Context, yield func(Path) error) error
```

EachPath executes a traversal ending in Path and calls yield for every Path. It returns ErrTraversalResult when the final pipeline step emits another type.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.Emit"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [Emit](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L401>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) Emit() *TraversalPipeline
```

Emit causes the active Repeat to emit the current element at each iteration, effectively returning intermediate results as well as final results. Emit is not a termination policy and must immediately follow Repeat or another repeat modifier.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.HasLabel"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [HasLabel](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L306>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) HasLabel(labels ...string) *TraversalPipeline
```

HasLabel filters the current node stream, keeping only nodes with one of the specified labels.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.IDs"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [IDs](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L483>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) IDs() *TraversalPipeline
```

IDs projects UUIDs from the current node stream. Unlike materializing nodes with ToNodes, this projection does not load node labels. Collect the result with ToIDs or stream it with EachID.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.In"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [In](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L293>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) In(labels ...string) *TraversalPipeline
```

In moves to incoming neighbor nodes, optionally filtering by edge label. Label filters use exact storage ranges. Multiple labels are deduplicated and returned in adjacency\-key order, independently of argument order.

Usage:

```
g.V().In("EMPLOYED_BY")...
```

<a name="TraversalPipeline.Out"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [Out](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L269>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) Out(labels ...string) *TraversalPipeline
```

Out moves to outgoing neighbor nodes, optionally filtering by edge label. Label filters use exact storage ranges. Multiple labels are deduplicated and returned in adjacency\-key order, independently of argument order.

Usage:

```
g.V().Out("KNOWS")...
```

<a name="TraversalPipeline.Path"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [Path](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L466>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) Path() *TraversalPipeline
```

Path transforms the current stream into immutable Path values containing the ordered nodes and edges visited for each result. Collect them with ToPaths or stream them with EachPath. Usage:

```
g.V().Out().Path()
```

<a name="TraversalPipeline.Repeat"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [Repeat](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L361>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) Repeat(sub func(*TraversalPipeline) *TraversalPipeline) *TraversalPipeline
```

Repeat compiles and repeatedly executes the provided sub\-traversal in breadth\-first order. The body must extend and return its input pipeline. Every Repeat must be terminated with Until or Times unless AllowUnboundedRepeat is explicitly selected. Nodes are deduplicated by UUID unless WithRepeatVisitMode selects RepeatPathSensitive.

Usage:

```
// 2-hop friends
g.V().Repeat(func(t *TraversalPipeline) *TraversalPipeline {
	return t.Out("KNOWS")
}).Times(2)
```

<a name="TraversalPipeline.Times"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [Times](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L375>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) Times(n int) *TraversalPipeline
```

Times terminates the active Repeat after n iterations. It must immediately follow Repeat or another repeat modifier, and n must be positive. Invalid configuration returns ErrInvalidRepeat when the traversal executes.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToEdges"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToEdges](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L716>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToEdges() ([]Edge, error)
```

ToEdges executes an edge traversal and returns its materialized Edge values. It returns ErrTraversalResult when the final pipeline step emits another type. Use EachEdge to consume large edge result sets with bounded memory.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToEdgesContext"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToEdgesContext](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L721>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToEdgesContext(ctx context.Context) ([]Edge, error)
```

ToEdgesContext is ToEdges with cancellation and observability context.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToIDs"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToIDs](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L740>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToIDs() ([]uuid.UUID, error)
```

ToIDs executes a traversal ending in IDs and returns typed UUID values. It returns ErrTraversalResult when the final pipeline step emits another type. Use EachID to consume large ID result sets with bounded memory.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToIDsContext"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToIDsContext](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L745>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToIDsContext(ctx context.Context) ([]uuid.UUID, error)
```

ToIDsContext is ToIDs with cancellation and observability context.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToList"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToList](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L675>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToList() (results []any, err error)
```

ToList executes the traversal pipeline and returns dynamic materialized results. Nodes use Node, edges use Edge, IDs uses uuid.UUID, Path uses Path, and Values uses the property types documented by Predicate. Prefer ToNodes, ToEdges, ToIDs, or ToPaths for statically typed results. To consume dynamic results with bounded memory, use Each.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToListContext"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToListContext](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L682>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToListContext(ctx context.Context) (results []any, err error)
```

ToListContext executes the traversal pipeline with ctx and returns materialized results. Cancellation stops planning, reads, scans, repeats, and result collection, and is propagated to observability hooks.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToNodes"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToNodes](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L704>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToNodes() ([]Node, error)
```

ToNodes executes a node traversal and returns its materialized Node values. It returns ErrTraversalResult when the final pipeline step emits another type. Use EachNode to consume large node result sets with bounded memory.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToNodesContext"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToNodesContext](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L709>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToNodesContext(ctx context.Context) ([]Node, error)
```

ToNodesContext is ToNodes with cancellation and observability context.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToPaths"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToPaths](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L728>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToPaths() ([]Path, error)
```

ToPaths executes a traversal ending in Path and returns typed path snapshots. It returns ErrTraversalResult when the final pipeline step emits another type. Use EachPath to consume large path result sets with bounded memory.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.ToPathsContext"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [ToPathsContext](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L733>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) ToPathsContext(ctx context.Context) ([]Path, error)
```

ToPathsContext is ToPaths with cancellation and observability context.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.Until"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [Until](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L325>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) Until(pred NodePredicate) *TraversalPipeline
```

Until terminates the active Repeat when pred returns true for the current materialized Node. It must immediately follow Repeat or another repeat modifier. A nil predicate or invalid ordering returns ErrInvalidRepeat when the traversal executes.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.Values"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [Values](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L494>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) Values(keys ...string) *TraversalPipeline
```

Values projects properties from the current elements. It emits one typed scalar per requested key, in key order. Missing properties are omitted, and calling Values without keys produces an empty result stream.

<a name="TraversalPipeline.WithRepeatVisitMode"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalPipeline\) [WithRepeatVisitMode](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L420>)

```go
func (tp *TraversalPipeline) WithRepeatVisitMode(mode RepeatVisitMode) *TraversalPipeline
```

WithRepeatVisitMode selects how the active Repeat handles converging paths. RepeatDeduplicateNodes is the default and visits each UUID once; RepeatPathSensitive preserves distinct simple paths while suppressing cycles within each path. It must immediately follow Repeat or another repeat modifier and may be specified only once.

<a name="TraversalSource"></a>
## type [TraversalSource](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L55-L57>)

TraversalSource is the starting point for graph traversals. It holds a reference to the database and spawns TraversalPipelines.

```go
type TraversalSource struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="NewTraversalSource"></a>
### func [NewTraversalSource](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L64>)

```go
func NewTraversalSource(db *Database) *TraversalSource
```

NewTraversalSource creates a new traversal source from a database instance.

Usage:

```
g := pathway.NewTraversalSource(db)
```

<a name="TraversalSource.V"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalSource\) [V](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L79>)

```go
func (ts *TraversalSource) V(ids ...uuid.UUID) *TraversalPipeline
```

V starts a traversal. If ids are provided, it starts at the specified nodes. If no ids are provided, it starts a scan of all nodes in the graph.

Usage:

```
// Start at specific node
g.V(id).Out()...

// Start at all nodes (scan)
g.V().HasLabel("Person")...
```

<a name="TraversalSource.VExternal"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalSource\) [VExternal](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L113>)

```go
func (ts *TraversalSource) VExternal(ids ...ExternalID) (*TraversalPipeline, error)
```

VExternal resolves external identities and starts a traversal at their internal nodes, preserving caller order and skipping unbound identities. An empty argument list scans all nodes, matching V. Each external start adds a forward lookup and reverse\-consistency check before normal node loading.

<a name="TraversalSource.VStrings"></a>
### func \(\*TraversalSource\) [VStrings](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/query.go#L97>)

```go
func (ts *TraversalSource) VStrings(ids ...string) (*TraversalPipeline, error)
```

VStrings parses textual UUIDs and starts a traversal at those nodes. It returns ErrInvalidNodeID if any value is malformed; no partial traversal is constructed. Prefer V when UUIDs are already available.

<a name="Tx"></a>
## type [Tx](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L17-L26>)

Tx represents a database transaction. It can be either read\-only \(created via View\) or read\-write \(created via Update\).

```go
type Tx struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Tx.Access"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [Access](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L157>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) Access(fn func(tx *Tx) error) error
```

Access allows executing a function within the transaction context. Useful for executing multiple operations on the same transaction \(e.g. Iterators\).

<a name="Tx.BindExternalID"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [BindExternalID](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/external_id_tx.go#L23>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) BindExternalID(externalID ExternalID, nodeID uuid.UUID) error
```

BindExternalID atomically binds externalID to an existing node. Repeating the same binding is idempotent. Binding an existing external ID to a different node returns ErrExternalIDConflict.

<a name="Tx.Close"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [Close](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L165>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) Close() error
```

Close closes the transaction. This releases the underlying snapshot. For write transactions \(Update\), it's a no\-op as the batch is managed by the DB.Update method, but for read\-only \(View/NewReadTx\), it releases the read lease.

<a name="Tx.Delete"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [Delete](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L148>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) Delete(key []byte, opts *pebble.WriteOptions) error
```

Delete deletes the raw value for a given key. Returns an error if the transaction is read\-only.

<a name="Tx.DeleteEdge"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [DeleteEdge](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L470>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) DeleteEdge(edgeID uuid.UUID) error
```

DeleteEdge removes a specific edge, including both adjacency records, its reverse\-index record, and its properties.

<a name="Tx.DeleteNode"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [DeleteNode](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L395>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) DeleteNode(id uuid.UUID) error
```

DeleteNode deletes a node and all its incident edges \(both outgoing and incoming\), including each edge's reverse\-index entry and properties. Its cost is linear in the node's degree.

<a name="Tx.FindNodes"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [FindNodes](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L660>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) FindNodes(label, propKey string, propValue interface{}) NodeIterator
```

FindNodes performs an exact typed lookup in a node\-property index configured through Options.Indexes. An unindexed label/property pair returns no results. String, numeric, and boolean values are distinct; value prefixes do not match. The iterator reports an encoding error if label or propKey exceeds 65,535 bytes.

<a name="Tx.Get"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [Get](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L102>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) Get(key []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

Get retrieves the raw value for a given key. It handles the difference between read\-only readers and write batches.

<a name="Tx.GetNode"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [GetNode](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L548>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) GetNode(id uuid.UUID) (string, bool, error)
```

GetNode retrieves a node's label by its ID. Returns the label, a boolean indicating existence, and any error.

<a name="Tx.GetProperties"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [GetProperties](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L567>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) GetProperties(id uuid.UUID) (map[string]interface{}, error)
```

GetProperties retrieves the properties map for a given node or edge ID. Signed integers are returned as int64, unsigned integers as uint64, and floats as float64. Returns nil if no properties exist.

<a name="Tx.InEdges"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [InEdges](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L607>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) InEdges(id uuid.UUID, labels ...string) EdgeIterator
```

InEdges returns incoming edges to id. When labels are provided, each unique label is read through an exact Pebble range. Results use adjacency\-key order, independently of the order in which labels are supplied.

<a name="Tx.Load"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [Load](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/ogm.go#L13>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) Load(id uuid.UUID, dest interface{}) error
```

Load populates the destination struct with properties from the node/edge with the given ID. dest must be a pointer to a struct.

<a name="Tx.OutEdges"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [OutEdges](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L595>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) OutEdges(id uuid.UUID, labels ...string) EdgeIterator
```

OutEdges returns outgoing edges from id. When labels are provided, each unique label is read through an exact Pebble range. Results use adjacency\-key order, independently of the order in which labels are supplied.

Usage:

```
iter := tx.OutEdges(nodeID, "KNOWS", "WORKS_WITH")
defer iter.Close()
for iter.Next() { ... }
```

<a name="Tx.PutEdge"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [PutEdge](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L248>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) PutEdge(srcID, dstID uuid.UUID, label string) (uuid.UUID, error)
```

PutEdge creates a directed edge between two existing nodes. Endpoint checks test key existence without copying or decoding node labels. Pathway uses multigraph semantics: every call creates a distinct edge, even when the endpoints and label match an existing edge. It performs a dual\-write, creating both an outgoing key \(for traversals from source\) and an incoming key \(for traversals to target\).

Returns an error if either source or destination node does not exist.

Usage:

```
edgeID, err := tx.PutEdge(srcID, dstID, "KNOWS")
```

<a name="Tx.PutNode"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [PutNode](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L183>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) PutNode(id uuid.UUID, label string) error
```

PutNode creates or updates a node with the given label. Changing an existing node's label migrates its configured property\-index entries.

Usage:

```
id := uuid.New()
err := tx.PutNode(id, "Person")
```

<a name="Tx.PutNodeByExternalID"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [PutNodeByExternalID](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/external_id_tx.go#L79>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) PutNodeByExternalID(externalID ExternalID, label string) (uuid.UUID, error)
```

PutNodeByExternalID atomically resolves or creates the node identified by externalID, updates its label, and returns its stable internal UUID. Repeated imports of the same external ID are idempotent.

<a name="Tx.ResolveExternalID"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [ResolveExternalID](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/external_id_tx.go#L16>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) ResolveExternalID(externalID ExternalID) (uuid.UUID, bool, error)
```

ResolveExternalID returns the internal UUID bound to externalID. The boolean is false when no binding exists. Dangling or inconsistent forward/reverse records return ErrExternalIDCorrupt.

```go
func (tx *Tx) ScanNodes() NodeIterator
```

ScanNodes scans all nodes in the database. This is a full table scan and can be slow for large datasets.

<a name="Tx.SetProperties"></a>
### func \(\*Tx\) [SetProperties](<https://github.com/npclaudiu/pathway/blob/main/tx.go#L318>)

```go
func (tx *Tx) SetProperties(id uuid.UUID, props map[string]interface{}) error
```

SetProperties sets a map of properties for an existing node or edge. This completely replaces any existing properties for that entity. It returns ErrEntityNotFound if id identifies neither kind of entity. Signed integers are stored and returned as int64, unsigned integers as uint64, floats as float64, and byte slices remain byte slices. Lists and nested maps recursively support the same property value types.

Usage:

```
err := tx.SetProperties(id, map[string]interface{}{
    "name": "Alice",
    "age":  30,
})
```


UnbindExternalID atomically removes an external\-ID binding. Removing a binding that does not exist succeeds.
